items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was playing with Dave Barbour on guitar and Jimmie Rowles on piano.

ctx.x: Yeah. I came to California. Ted FioRito was in a place called the Florentine Gardens. The Mills Brothers were the main attraction there. You talk about learning something. Harry, [?] – all four of them, actually. Their father was still living. But they were the class act. They taught me more about music than anybody else, being available at Florentine Gardens. It was three months there at Florentine Gardens. While I was there, they had a pickpocket, a guy by the name of Dr. Giovanni. He had somebody come up, and…
An amazing story. Did he even talk to you? Did he ever say anything to you?

items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: I don't know whether it was Buddy Rich or Louis Bellson

ctx.x: was doing a Norman Granz concert, and he turned around, and he went to the drummer, I don't know whether it was Buddy Rich or Louis Bellson, but he said, "When Prez plays, just give me titty-boom. I don't want a whole bunch of bombs and stuff. Just titty-boom." And that's the way he used to be when I worked with him. He was so easy to play with. He was a monstrosity. I couldn't believe him.
We had a cooking contest one time. It was Lester, Bumps, Lady Day, my wife Dorothy, and I think Louis was there, Louis Gonzalez, the guitar player, and Paul...
